checks.finding: The amendment's new third exception is stated in terms no implementer can evaluate. (1) requirements.md:389-397 and AC-012 (requirements.md:833) key the exception on 'the invocation's own transient staging area is found to resolve outside this feature's own fixed publication write set', but 'fixed publication write set' is defined nowhere: REQ-002 says the set is 'immediately below' (requirements.md:395 -- nothing below it in REQ-002 states a write set; the write boundary appears only in Security Boundaries, requirements.md:1153-1160), while AC-012 says it is 'REQ-001's fixed write set' (requirements.md:833), and REQ-001 states only a 'track-exclusive output set' of published artifacts {facet-manifest.yaml, project-context.resolved.json, resolver-evidence.yaml} / {capability-summary.yaml, resolver-evidence.yaml} (requirements.md:318-320). The two cross-references point at different sections and neither defines the term. (2) Under the only enumerated set, the staging area specs/<feature>/.resolver-staging/ (requirements.md:1157) is by construction NOT a member -- Security Boundaries lists it separately and calls it 'never a live path itself' -- so the predicate reads as universally true, collapsing a stated 'sub-case' into every publication-journal-recovery Block. (3) No requirement says when containment is evaluated, what 'resolve' means (realpath/symlink vs lexical), or which step performs it; REQ-002's publication-journal-recovery row (requirements.md:356) enumerates exactly two unrecoverable conditions (missing/unreadable pre-image backup; live hash matching neither PRE nor POST), neither of which is an uncontained staging area, in a taxonomy the spec declares 'closed at sixteen rows' and machine-readable (requirements.md:346-351). (4) acceptance-tests.md:86 (AC-047/TEST-047) now asserts the recovery algorithm leaves targets 'exactly as found ... in contrast to its MIX outcome, which deliberately does restore them'; 'MIX' and the 'four-outcome enumeration' occur exactly once in the entire Phase-1 pair (that clause) and are explicitly deferred to design.md, while requirements.md:258-260 and :1146-1148 describe only TWO terminal states. Downstream failure mode: a Phase-2 implementer and a fixture author cannot decide when this Block fires, what containment check to implement, or which recovery outcomes restore targets -- two implementers would reasonably build different behavior or none at all. This is spec-review scope because REQ-002's Block taxonomy and its exception list are the specification's own product behavior, not an implementation detail. Major per the calibration: an ambiguous requirement that will cause downstream mismatch.

The 2026-08-27 amendment widened the Evidence-on-every-Block exception list in two places but left at least two sibling normative statements asserting the opposite. (1) requirements.md:383-397 (REQ-002 closing paragraph) now names THREE exceptions, the third writing no live artifact at all; but REQ-004 at requirements.md:564-568 still states Resolver Evidence 'is written on **every** invocation, success or Block (REQ-002), **with the sole exception of a Block reached because Resolver Evidence itself fails its own schema self-validation** (B3, revised -- that one case writes nothing at all...)'. 'Sole exception' plus 'that one case writes nothing at all' is now false: two cases write nothing. The phrasing was precise before the amendment (disabled-legacy-invocation still writes a minimal record, so it was correctly not an exception to writing), which confirms the conflict is a genuine un-propagated change rather than loose wording. (2) Security Boundaries at requirements.md:1176-1184 still guarantees that every path is left 'fully absent, fully unchanged ..., or (Resolver Evidence only, on a Block reached before publication) fully written' -- the new sub-case is detected at REQ-001 step 0 (requirements.md:255-261), i.e. before publication, yet writes nothing. (3) The amendment's own stated justification -- 'writing Evidence in that sub-case is structurally impossible: the write would itself have to pass through the very staging area just found to be uncontained' (requirements.md:392-395; repeated acceptance-tests.md:54) -- is contradicted by Main Workflows 4 (requirements.md:1026), where minimal Resolver Evidence is 'written directly (no staging area ever exists in this branch)'. The package therefore already contains a non-staged Evidence write path, so the impossibility premise the exception rests on is denied by the package's own text. Downstream failure mode: an implementer following REQ-004/Security Boundaries writes an Evidence record on this Block; one following REQ-002/AC-012 writes nothing; the two produce opposite live-filesystem state for the identical fail-closed Block, and a fixture author cannot decide which assertion to encode. Critical: this is a direct conflict on a fail-closed, safety-relevant write rule, not a clarification.

The amendment introduces a new failure condition -- this invocation's transient staging area resolving outside the permitted write set (requirements.md:389-391) -- but scopes both its detection and its handling to a sub-case of one diagnostic reached only when a stale journal is also present. No acceptance criterion or test row covers the identical condition on any other path: not on a successful Full-track or Lite-track resolve (Main Workflows 1/2, requirements.md:971-1007), not on any of the other fifteen Block rows, and not on an invocation with no stale journal at all -- even though every publication is routed through that staging area (REQ-001 step (m), requirements.md:317-332) and Security Boundaries asserts the Resolver 'never ... writes outside' the enumerated paths (requirements.md:1153-1160). The sixteen-row closed enum (requirements.md:353-370) contains no diagnostic for an uncontained staging area outside this sub-case, so on the un-covered paths the specified behaviour is to write through it. Separately, the one fixture obligation that was added -- acceptance-tests.md:54 ('its fixture asserts the canonical diagnostic line is emitted and that no Resolver Evidence and no other live artifact is written') -- cannot be authored, because the trigger it must construct is unspecified (see AMBIGUITY), and AC-010/TEST-010's per-row fixture for publication-journal-recovery (acceptance-tests.md:52, AC-047 at :86) is the corrupted-pre-image case, not this one. Downstream failure mode: a verifier has no way to build the negative-path fixture the amendment mandates, and the write-boundary violation the amendment concedes is possible remains untested on every non-recovery path. Major: a missing observable acceptance surface for a materially unsafe negative path the requirements themselves now imply.

Every assumption is either resolved by investigation or carries an explicit, owned pre-design/pre-implementation decision path. requirements.md:1214-1222 binds the four sibling-contract dependencies to their already-Passed states with a named follow-up obligation if any changes (investigation.md INV-004). requirements.md:1223-1237 states the two live-repository snapshots (guard reservation for resolve-project-context.*, INV-003; SKILL.md protection status, INV-017) as re-verified-at-task-start facts with a stated alternative sequencing rather than silent reliance. Open Questions (requirements.md:1239-1259): OQ-001/OQ-002 are explicitly deferred to a named future caller/epic and are outside this feature's scope per Non-goals (requirements.md:769-771); OQ-003 is recorded resolved with a concrete file:line anchor plus a position-sensitive drift check (AC-053, requirements.md:874). The one genuinely unresolved cross-epic gap -- no Registry field to source required_lite_checks -- is named with an explicit owner (Epic A2 maintainers), an explicit scope, a migration note, and a fail-closed consequence (requirements.md:139-163, :1263-1293; investigation.md INV-019), and Non-goals refuses to fabricate a source (requirements.md:757-761). Nothing here forces the design or task author to guess at an unstated assumption.

The change under review asserts a human approval that the package's own approval record does not contain. requirements.md:391, requirements.md:833 (AC-012), acceptance-tests.md:54 and acceptance-tests.md:86 each ground a normative change in 'amended 2026-08-27, human-approved, ruling option 4'. Every earlier amendment in this package supplies a conforming, citable record and is pointed at from the amended text: the 2026-08-24 A(1)/B(1) lineage (investigation.md:800-887 -- full commit hashes, per-document SHA-256, verbatim dated quotations) and the 2026-08-26 C(1)/C(2) lineage (investigation.md:1214-1343), with explicit 'approval evidence: investigation.md ## Amendment Re-Review Context > ### Rulings C(1)/C(2)' pointers embedded in requirements.md:364 and :368. For the 2026-08-27 amendment there is no such entry at all: investigation.md contains no occurrence of '2026-08-27', no 'option 4', no commit pin for the amendment, no per-document SHA-256 for the amended bytes, and no verbatim dated approval quotation; the record's most recent pins (investigation.md:1335 requirements.md=1028bf2c..., :1340 acceptance-tests.md=a9fa4f89...) do not match the bytes under review (precheck-result.json:8-9 = 0f8837e3..., 49e02209...). 'Ruling option 4' is additionally a reference to an enumeration of options that appears nowhere in the reviewed package, so even the content of what was approved is unrecoverable from the artifacts. The calibration's amendment-lane evidence bar (elements 1, 2 and 3) is therefore unmet for this amendment, and its authority reduces to a bare self-declaration inside the very documents it authorizes. Downstream failure mode: no reviewer, task author, or verifier can test whether the removal of a fail-closed Evidence obligation was actually sanctioned, or reconstruct its scope. Spec-review scope: the amendment approval record is a Phase-1 artifact (investigation.md) and an input to this gate. Critical: a governance boundary the specification itself invokes is not testable for the bytes being reviewed. Remedy is mechanical -- append a conforming '## Amendment Re-Review Context' entry for commit fa1ad0e0 with the full hash, the post-amendment SHA-256 of requirements.md/acceptance-tests.md, and the verbatim dated approval quotation, and add the same approval-evidence pointer the C(1)/C(2) rows already carry.

Two independent handoff blockers. (a) Product behaviour must be invented: as recorded under CONTRADICTION and AMBIGUITY, the design/implementation-policy reviewer would have to decide on their own whether Resolver Evidence is written on the new publication-journal-recovery sub-case (REQ-004 requirements.md:564-568 and Security Boundaries :1183-1184 say yes; REQ-002 :389-397 and AC-012 :833 say no), what 'resolves outside the fixed publication write set' means operationally, and at which step the containment check runs -- none of which is a design decision the spec legitimately defers, since all three are the Block taxonomy's own semantics. (b) The authoritative acceptance-criterion set is not determinable from the Phase-1 pair: acceptance-tests.md:3-18 declares an AC-NNN<->TEST-NNN 1:1 mapping with exactly one documented exception class (AC-035/036/037), and its preamble (acceptance-tests.md:29-39) enumerates the new rows as 'AC-038 through AC-056'; yet acceptance-tests.md carries AC-057 (line 97) and AC-058 (line 98), which have no counterpart rows in requirements.md's Acceptance Criteria table -- that table ends at AC-056 (requirements.md:877) -- while requirements.md:364 and :368 cite AC-058 and AC-057 as if they existed there. Those two rows are also separated from the table by a blank line (acceptance-tests.md:96) and carry no header row, so they are not part of the preceding Markdown table and will not be extracted by any row-wise reader. A task author or traceability generator cannot decide whether this feature has 56 or 58 acceptance criteria, and the two rows covering the C(1)/C(2) Block sub-triggers are the ones at risk of being dropped. Major: unbounded/undecidable inputs to task decomposition and traceability, plus product behaviour a later gate would have to invent.
